title: Swapping pair components is polynomial-time
statement: Let $\langle x,y\rangle$ denote the bit string formed by doubling each bit of $x$, appending the separator $01$, and then appending $y$. The map that sends a bit string $z$ to the encoding of its total second projection followed by its total first projection is polynomial-time computable; either projection is the empty word when parsing fails.
replaced: Let $\langle a,b\rangle$ denote the self-delimiting pair encoding of bit strings $a$ and $b$ (every bit of $a$ doubled, then $01$, then $b$), and let $\pi_1$ and $\pi_2$ be the total projections, which send $\langle a,b\rangle$ to $a$ and to $b$ respectively, and any bit string that is not a pair encoding to the empty word. Then the map $z \mapsto \langle \pi_2(z), \pi_1(z)\rangle$ is polynomial-time computable.
